citation_system: theory file and the Isabelle name of the axiom, definition, theorem or lemma (e.g. GoedelGod.thy, A1a; GoedelGod.thy, T3), as in the AFP release of 2026-02-06 (Isabelle2025-2)
notes: Formalization reference for Scott's variant (#134), BSD license. Pinned as the web snapshot AFP-GOEDELGOD-THY of the AFP's HTML rendering of GoedelGod.thy, because the source kinds are frozen (AGENTS.md invariant 18) and a text witness must be XML. The rendered theory is the one in the AFP release tarball afp-GoedelGod-2026-02-06.tar.gz (sha256 1a907c6e705009ebe67a3e30d0e550b9d94f8d12b9d4d93258f74347a442b031; GoedelGod/GoedelGod.thy sha256 6a9e3d58c51754c9ccb86d94762a076c133df36aca4aa2d5b046d76b4f4d011a, Git blob 938bc64cb9ce48c1b1853d64ab2594b8ba64b43b), which was also the current release when pinned. The page lives under browser_info/current/ and is regenerated by each AFP release; the only Wayback capture (2024-11-27) extracts to different text, so none is recorded, and the snapshot must be re-pinned (and its claims re-read) when a release changes the page. The theory is a secondary witness for Scott's notes, which the theory cites as 'Appendix B: Notes in Dana Scott's Hand' in J. H. Sobel, Logic and Theism, pp. 145-146, which are not pinned. Claims attribute what the AFP theory states. They do not say what Gödel or Scott intended, and a proof of a theorem of the theory does not establish that.
